title.narrative: Output 6.3. Increased capacity of member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative:
The Government developed an action plan, which included various steps towards ratification and implementation of C190.
a) The Minister of Labour, Industrial Relations and Employment Creation (MLIREC) established a Working Group (WG) on Violence and Harassment at management level. This WG is in charge or supervising work related to violence and harassment in the Ministry. A Tripartite Task Force under the Labour Advisory Committee (LAC) has been established and is reviewing the Labour Act, 2007 with a view to develop amendments that will integrate the provisions of C190. The Tripartite Taskforce recommended C190 for ratification to the Minister of Labour.
b) Taking advantage of an upcoming labour law reforms, MLIREC submitted specific proposals on provisions relating to C190, as follows: 1. violence and harassment is included as a fundamental right at work; 2. under provisions related to OSH, the scope is expanded to include violence and harassment and its associated risks.
c) In November 2021, tripartite partners adopted a Training Manual on violence and harassment that will be used by trainers drawn from the tripartite partners and world of work actors in their information sharing, advocacy and training of gender champions in the world of work.
d) MLIREC organised several training and awareness-raising programmes. This resulted in strengthened capacity of public officials and social partners. For instance, a High-Level Briefing on C190 for Government, Social Partners, State-owned Enterprises, Informal Sector and Media Editors was organised in February 2020, to fully understand the scope and obligations under C190. Moreover, 10 Master Trainers and 200 Trainer of Trainers from tripartite plus constituencies have been trained from September to November 2021. Finally, a series of short interactive graphic videos have been designed as a key component of the nation-wide awareness campaign on the elimination of violence and harassment. Throughout the biennium, the ILO has provided extensive support to tripartite constituents in Namibia. In particular, the ILO facilitated and supported the organisation of the High-Level Briefing on C190 for Government, Social Partners, State-owned Enterprises, Informal Sector, Private Sectors and Media Editors. It also supported the development of the training materials and training of master and trainer of trainers, by providing both financial and technical support.
The ILO also supported Government’s efforts related to C190 advocacy and sensitisation activities, particularly following the ratification of the Convention by Namibia by sharing the texts of C190 with key stakeholders including the tripartite partners, UN Country Team and the media.
